reasons: The replacement theorem is strictly stronger, treats arbitrary \(D,D'\in\mathfrak D\), and removes the obsolete reference-graph and rational-separation framing. Deletion with a replacement preserves inbound dependency migration without misclassifying the strengthening as a narrowing.
Classwise inference requires an explicit symbol for a fixed returned maximal-effect quotient class.
The derivative must be indexed by the selected fixed representative circuit.
The exact confidence quantile and the numerical 1.96 corollary use the standard normal distribution function.
Every quotient class needs a deterministic representative whose observable circuit is evaluated.
The sandwich covariance must be computed from the fixed class-representative circuit.
The strengthened theorem reports inference for an arbitrary fixed linear contrast.
The general Wald statement requires an arbitrary nominal miscoverage level.
The coordinate variance must record which returned quotient-class circuit is used.
The classwise circuit is a new indexed object; retaining the existing unindexed one-class circuit keeps earlier equality-branch statements coherent.
The plug-in estimator must carry the fixed quotient-class index.
The estimator and covariance must be defined for every fixed returned quotient class and must state the sample-independent certification condition used by the theorem.
target-estimand-replace: The estimand line must expose both the maximal pairwise quotient and the class-specific causal vectors covered by fixed-class inference.
estimand-functional-replace: The previous line advertised only the common one-class circuit and did not state the class-indexed target or the fixed-class scope of inference.

comparator-promise-table-replace: The comparison record must distinguish fixed-class Wald inference from Chang--Guo--Malinsky post-selection coverage while preserving the existing graphical comparator scopes.

The theorem is synchronized with the class-indexed estimator and states the fixed-class causal equality, multivariate limit, sandwich consistency, arbitrary fixed-contrast Wald interval, numerical coordinate corollary, and selection scope required by the active directive.

narrow: The existing claim leaves the inferential status of a quotient class implicit and does not exclude reuse of the inference sample for oracle or class selection. The replacement narrows the coverage guarantee to a population-fixed or externally certified true class independent of the inference sample, while carrying the same proved fixed-circuit argument to every returned class and exposing its fixed-contrast Wald consequence as required by the active directive.

verdict.note: Accepted 13 sound pairwise theorem/estimator items; rejected meta and classwise CLT pending global-Markov and u_star schema repairs.
